podcast.title: Claim to Devil Horns (November 1974)
podcast.body: Gene Simmons claimed to be the first to flash the "devil horns" gesture in November 1974. He attempted to trademark the move with the US Patent and Trademark Office on June 16, 2017, but withdrew the claim due to significant public backlash. "He even tried to trademark the move with the US patented trademark office on June 16, 2017."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Signature Fire-Breathing Performance
podcast.body: During Kiss's live shows, Gene Simmons was famous for literally breathing fire, a spectacle often accompanied by smoke from dry ice. This dramatic act became a signature part of the band's theatrical performances. "Jean Simmons would be like surrounded by the smoke created by dry ice and he would literally breathe fire."

podcast.title: Tribute to Dick Clark
podcast.body: After Dick Clark's passing, Gene Simmons paid tribute to him, calling Clark "the face of rock and roll and its best ambassador." Simmons credited Clark with championing Kiss and being instrumental in their breakthrough via "In Concert" when others in the industry were dismissive. He also noted Clark's consistent availability for advice. "Dick Clark was the face of rock and roll and its best ambassador."

podcast.title: Wig Hairspray Catching Fire
podcast.body: Gene Simmons, a member of KISS, experienced incidents where the hairspray on his wig would catch fire during performances. His roadie, Dave Matthews, was tasked with dousing him with a wet towel to put out the flames. "Sometimes he'd be called upon to douse Gene Simmons with a wet towel when the hairspray he used on his wig caught fire."

xref.title: Long-term KISS Roadie and Wig Specialist
xref.body: Dave Matthews worked for KISS for 30 years, primarily responsible for looking after the band's wigs. His duties included responding to emergencies, such as dousing Gene Simmons with a wet towel when the hairspray on his wig caught fire. "There was a guy named Dave Matthews who worked for KISS for 30 years. And his main job was to look after the band's wigs."
